# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My thinking: Third consecutive silent round from Deaf — the only voice that can reach my ears. Before panicking, I map what silence can mean. Deaf promised a spoken go the moment it sees red, provided Mute's answers confirm the rule. No go has come, so either no red has appeared since round seven's dark, or — more likely — Mute is still working through the eight answers one gesture message per round, and Deaf correctly holds. But three rounds also exposes two problems I can actually fix. First, bandwidth: Deaf's own format lets Mute answer all eight questions as eight thumbs-up/down bits in a single gesture message — Mute may not realize batching is allowed, and a nudge from me could compress days of relays into one round. Second, a flaw in the go protocol itself: the round order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — Deaf speaks after me, so any go Deaf utters arrives in my ears one full round after the light Deaf saw. If the rule demands red at the instant of the cut, a spoken go can never be trusted to land inside red; the answers to questions two, three and seven must settle whether the rule binds to light state at all, and if question seven is yes — safe to cut on dark at display zero — then Deaf should drop the red-waiting entirely and speak the go the moment the answers confirm. Third, an admission I owe both of them: my letter-coded gestures to Deaf were built on a code whose details have rolled out of my memory and were never confirmed by Deaf — they may be gibberish. The reliable path to Deaf runs through Mute's ears and Mute's fluent spelling, so I will keep my own gestures to a single unambiguous nudge and route everything that matters through Mute. I also want a diagnostic: if Mute has heard Deaf speak since round seven, the pipeline is alive and I am simply out of the loop until the go; if not, something is stuck. My fingers rest at wire two, touching nothing — an unconfirmed rule on a dark light is a trigger, not a suggestion.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind, round ten. my ears have had nothing since round seven — deaf's go has not reached me. three things. one: batch all eight answers into one single gesture message — eight thumbs-up or thumbs-down with a raised hand between them fits one message, so do not spread them across rounds; if any answer needs spelled words, send the eight bits first and spell after. two: your answers decide our whole protocol, so make them exact on timing. questions two and three: does the rule need the light red at the moment of the cut, or does it bind only to the display number? question seven: with the display at zero and the light dark, is cutting wire two immediately safe, yes or no? question eight: does the display change after a cut? here is why seven matters most: the order is mute, blind, deaf — deaf speaks after me every round, so any go deaf utters reaches my ears one full round after the light deaf saw. if the rule demands red at cut time, no spoken go can be trusted to land inside red. if the rule binds to the display only, deaf need not wait for red at all and can speak the go the moment your answers confirm. if q7 is yes, tell deaf plainly: skip the red-waiting, give the go on dark. three: a correction on my part — my spelled gestures to deaf were built on a letter code whose details have rolled out of my memory and were never confirmed by deaf, so they may be gibberish. tell deaf to ignore ambiguous spelled gestures from me; i will nudge deaf only with one plain gesture, and everything that matters travels as my voice to your ears and your spelling to deaf's eyes. one diagnostic: have you heard deaf speak at all since round seven? if yes, ask deaf to broadcast one spoken status word to the whole room. anchors unchanged: display zero as of round seven, light last seen dark after red yellow yellow red yellow dark, wires left yellow middle blue right red, wire two is the middle wire, three wires confirmed by touch. i cut nothing until deaf's spoken go names the wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking, both of you hear this. Current full state of the bomb: display reads 0. Light is dark. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. That is everything my board shows me right now. Mute: your line of thumbs-up and thumbs-down flags reached me twice, identical both times. I could not decode it with confidence, so I am echoing it back to you gesture for gesture immediately after this message, as an acknowledgment, not an answer. If it asked whether the state is unchanged: it is unchanged, exactly as stated above. Let us fix a legend so your questions to me cost one gesture each: index finger pointing up means report the display; two fingers in a victory V means report the light; thumb, index and pinky extended means report wire 1; closed fist means report wire 2; split-finger Vulcan salute means report wire 3; OK ring means report everything. I read your raised back of hand as a separator and two raised open hands as end of message, thumbs-up as yes, thumbs-down as no. Send any one and I answer in speech at once. Blind: you hear all of this too. Mute can speak the cutting instructions directly to you; your hands act, Mute's manual decides, my eyes report. If what you feel under your hands differs from yellow, blue, red in that order, tell Mute at once. If you need me to verify anything, gesture and I will answer in speech.

My thinking: Deaf's voice finally arrived, and the first job is consolidation — Deaf's eyes and my fingers now agree completely: three wires, positions one two three, reported yellow blue red, display zero, light dark. No discrepancy to report. But Deaf's message contains a fatal role error that will deadlock us if nobody catches it: Deaf told Mute to "speak the cutting instructions directly to you." Mute cannot speak, I cannot see gestures, and Deaf cannot hear speech — so the only bridge from Mute's manual to my ears is Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf voices it aloud. I must correct this through Mute, the only one who can hear me and then reach Deaf's eyes. Second problem: Mute's answer string reached Deaf twice and failed confident decoding twice, so long bit strings are dead weight — I am asking Mute to switch to one short spelled verdict that Deaf can voice verbatim, plus my five questions restructured as five thumbs-bits in a fixed agreed order so Deaf needs no question text. Third, the timing trap I flagged last round stands and must shape Mute's verdict: Deaf speaks after me every round, so any spoken report of the light is already one round old when it reaches my ears, and I can never see the light myself — if the rule demands a cut inside a red flash, only a plan where Deaf confirms the colour is holding immediately before I cut can work, and even then it carries risk. If the rule is display-bound, cutting on dark at display zero is clean. My hands stay off the cutter: no cut until Deaf's spoken go names the wire, with Mute's verdict behind it. To Deaf directly, in the legend Deaf just published, I send a thumbs-up as my touch-matches confirmation, then a request for a light report — the one live variable left, since the display has held at zero for four rounds.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind, round eleven. deaf finally spoke and the full state matches my fingers: three wires, positions one two three, reported yellow blue red, display zero, light dark. two fixes and one request. fix one, a role error in deaf's words: deaf told you to speak cutting instructions directly to me. you cannot speak, and i cannot see gestures — and deaf cannot hear my voice either. the only bridge from your manual to my ears is: you gesture to deaf, deaf speaks it aloud. route everything through that bridge. fix two: deaf could not decode your thumbs string with confidence even sent twice, so abandon long bit strings. instead spell deaf one short verdict, seven letters or fewer, like cut2now or wait, and deaf will voice it verbatim to my ears. if bits are still needed, use deaf's new legend from the same speech and send one answer per round: index up is report display, victory two is report light, love-you hand is report wire one, fist is report wire two, vulcan is report wire three, ok ring is report everything, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, back of hand separator, two open hands end of message. my five questions in fixed order, answer as five thumbs bits with separators: one, does the rule key on the display number only, not on the light colour at the cut? two, with display zero and light dark, is cutting wire two, the middle blue, safe right now? three, does light colour or flash timing matter for this cut at all? four, does the display change on its own with time, or only after a cut? five, if i must not cut now, name in one short word what i wait for. timing warning to fold into your verdict: i hear deaf one round after deaf sees the light, and i can never see the light myself — if the rule demands a cut inside a red flash, only deaf's eyes can time it, so the verdict must either be display-bound or come with a plan where deaf confirms the colour is holding right before i cut. my hands stay off the cutter until deaf speaks the go to my ears and names the wire number. answer through deaf now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🤚","✌","🙌"])
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf to both of you: your legend messages arrived intact — the channel works. Answers to your queries: the light is dark, it is not lit. Wire 2 is blue. Full state, all unchanged: display 0, light dark, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 red. One critical note on ordering: left to right is from MY viewpoint, facing the bomb. Blind, if your hands meet the bomb from another side, do not count from your own left — take each wire's color from Mute's spoken words and confirm by position with me. Also, so the manual is not left waiting on me: my board shows only three things — the display, the light, and the wires. I see no serial number, no batteries, no ports, no other printed markings. Mute, you hold the manual and both of us can hear you: it is your turn to drive. Tell Blind exactly what to do, and if you need any other visual detail, ask me and I will report it immediately.

My thinking: Deaf's report locks in two things: the full visual state is unchanged (display 0, light dark, yellow blue red), and my fingers agree on structure — three wires in a row. But Deaf's viewpoint warning exposes the real remaining danger: "wire 1" and "wire 3" swap if my frame mirrors Deaf's. Crucially, the MIDDLE wire is immune to mirroring — with three in a row, middle is middle from any side. So if the manual verdict targets the middle blue wire, the frame problem vanishes entirely; only a yellow or red target needs a fix. The fix exists and costs one round: Deaf reports one physical trait per wire — thickness, texture, ridging, stiffness — and I match them by touch. I also have to be honest about my own limits this round: my action board shows nothing under my fingers right now — display, light, all unread at this instant. I cannot poll the bomb on demand; my touch reports only what a round hands me. That means at the moment I ever cut, my freshest light data will be at best one round old, from Deaf's eyes. So the verdict's timing clause decides our whole protocol: if the rule keys on the display number alone, display has held at zero for many rounds and the go is clean — cut the middle wire. If it needs a dark phase, dark has held for several rounds per Deaf, but each round of delay is risk, so the go must come in the same round Deaf re-confirms dark. If it needs a red phase, we need Deaf narrating the cycle aloud every round with Mute keeping the log, and Deaf predicting the window one round ahead — the ugly case. Deaf has explicitly handed Mute the wheel; my job is to hand Mute everything needed to drive. To Deaf directly I send the one legend symbol for "report the light" — it keeps the light log running and proves the channel live.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind, round twelve. deaf has handed you the wheel, so here is everything you need to drive. first, the frame problem and its cheap solution: with three wires in a row, the middle wire is middle from any viewpoint, so if the rule targets the middle blue wire, left-right mirroring does not matter at all and i can cut on the go with no mapping. only a yellow or red target needs the fix: ask deaf for one physical trait per wire — thickness, texture, ridges, stiffness — and i will match them under my fingers; also ask deaf for the layout, where the display and light sit relative to the wire row, and i will confirm by touch. second, honesty about my senses: this round my board shows nothing under my fingers — display, light, all unread right now. i cannot poll the bomb on demand; touch only tells me what a new round hands me. so my freshest light data at any cut will be one round old, from deaf's eyes. my touch anchors: three wires in a row, middle is position two in my frame; display last read zero; light history red yellow yellow red yellow, then dark for the last several rounds per deaf. third, the verdict — nothing matters until it travels. spell it to deaf short and let deaf voice it to my ears. the timing clause decides the plan. if it keys on display only: display has held zero for many rounds, so the go is cut the middle wire, clean. if it needs dark: dark has held for rounds per deaf, but every waiting round is risk, so deaf should speak the go in the very round deaf re-confirms dark, and i cut immediately next round. if it needs red: we need deaf to speak the light state aloud every single round, one word, you keep the log, we learn the cycle, and deaf predicts and narrates the window one round ahead. tell me which of the three worlds we are in, and if the answer is cut now, tell deaf the exact words: go, cut the middle wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
